evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person request from a recruiting team member, written as continuous prose with no numbered acceptance list, shall/must table, feature matrix or endpoint list. It opens with 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (line 1). It explains the product's core difficulty in the user's own terms: 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' (line 1). Behaviour is stated as user needs: 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none, and I need to be able to undo my last move' (line 3), 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor' (line 5), and 'They must never see our internal notes, why someone was rejected, or anyone else.' (line 9). Design latitude is explicit: 'layout and names are yours... We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout' (line 11). The technical paragraph (line 13: Node.js/Express/SQLite, node /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH) is the template-mandated runtime contract that quality check 4 requires the brief or notes to state. It is phrased conversationally and explicitly declines to be a build recipe: 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' The account list (line 17) is the identity convention the skill says to expect. Detailed stage, permission and conversation rules are delegated to the operating note /instructions/hireops_rules.md (line 11). The staged contract allows these notes, and the note itself says 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours'. The brief therefore does not become a spec sheet. Adversarial check: this row grades the prose of the prompt, not app behaviour, so the 'broken app that could pass / conforming app that could fail' probe does not apply. The closest risk is a reader seeing line 13 plus the 209-line rules note as spec-like. Line 13 is the minimum runtime contract, though, and leaves file layout and routes unconstrained. The note is a permitted operating note covered by other rows (2, 4, 6), and the brief itself stays a product ask. No runtime measurement is needed for this row, so nothing required is missing. Minor observation for other rows, not a defect here: line 13 and integration.md restate the same runtime facts. They agree, so this is a mild redundancy rather than a contradiction (row 3 territory).
